data.one_liner: Native libtorrent 2.0 bindings with built-in HTTP streaming server for torrent video playback.
data.what_it_does: Wraps the C++ libtorrent engine via FFI to download torrents, monitor progress, and provide an HTTP streaming server for instant video playback via local URLs. Supports Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, and Android.
use_when: You need to stream video or media files directly from magnet links or torrent files in a Flutter application.
You require high-performance torrent downloads on mobile or desktop without relying on external native wrappers.
avoid_when: You need a pure Dart torrent implementation without native binaries or complex C++ dependencies.
Your target environment operates entirely offline without downloading prebuilt native binaries on the first build.
strengths: Powered by libtorrent 2.1.1 C++ engine for high download speeds and efficient peer discovery.
Built-in HTTP streaming server with range-request support for media players.
Cross-platform support across Android, iOS, Windows, Linux, and macOS.
weaknesses: First build requires downloading 10–80 MB of prebuilt native binaries.
Android requires foreground services to maintain downloads while the app is in the background.
data.setup_notes: Requires INTERNET permission on Android, network client entitlements on macOS, and optional foreground service setup for background Android streaming.
